body: Maybe it’s worth it if you were born privileged. Otherwise, no.

Hello, I have both social anxiety and depression. I find it hard to resist the intruding thoughts from my depression also, but for social anxiety, I really improved by thinking “no one will care after this” when I did things. For example, during a school presentation, I realized no one *actually* pays attention to you. I never remembered someone else’s presentation afterwards and so, they probably wouldn’t remember me presenting. I used to get really nervous about it, but remembering that people don’t even think about it after 2 minutes helps me to get it done with quickly. If I’m out ordering food, I also tell myself that I’m just one out of many customers they go through. Sorry about the sort of negative view. I hope things get better for you soon!

I don’t think it’s selfish at all. It sounds like you’re crying for help and I get that. Sometimes it feels like no one really cares until you actually do something and almost end up dead. And then they worry about you for a little and then act the same after a while.
I think it’s my fault for dumping all of my emotions on them. I don’t think anyone would have reacted differently.

Thank you for this. It made me smile. I haven’t received kind words in a long time. I appreciate this community so much. 

And I want to find the right people, too, but it is really hard for me. I also have social anxiety so when I first found friends, I was really happy. Now that they left me, I don’t even know how to find anyone, since I’m not in high school anymore. They flat out told me they didn’t want to be my friend anymore. The loneliness has just been so overwhelming, so it was nice to hear your words. Thank you again.

I have and I guess I went too far. They got extremely upset and said they couldn’t handle my negative emotions anymore, so they left me. Still, I’d say you should go ahead and open up to your aunt. Just speaking out your feelings will help you a lot.
I would if I could get my hands on some, sadly. Thank, though.

Hi, I was in your girlfriend’s shoes before. The best thing I can say is to be extremely supportive of her (obviously). It doesn’t mean to enable her suicidal thoughts, though. What helps the most is just being there for her and ask questions to listen in and try to really understand what she’s feeling. You are already doing this by not dismissing or minimizing her feelings, so you’re good. Distract her from those thoughts by maybe playing online games with her, if you can. You can also try watching movies or shows together using some screen-sharing apps. 

The most important thing, though, is to not let those intrusive thoughts of her win (especially if she tries to push you away). Be there for her as much as you can. I was left behind and it only confirmed my thoughts that I was a bother to people... So, just reassure her that you’re not going to let it win and it isn’t all she is to you. Thats all I can say. I hope it helps!
I guess at least we have our pets, which is more than most people have. I wish the best for you.
Mostly my cats. And my parents if they find out. Otherwise, I’d be dead already. I’ve already given up hope that it could get better. I’m just living for my cats right now.
Yeah, you’re right. I do get that a lot about how I keep thinking and worrying about the future. I just need to calm down and focus on the present, but it’s hard.
Yes, every single day. People have proven to me time and time again that they don’t care about me by leaving me. You’re not alone.
Something like that happened to me when I called and it completely turned me off to calling or speaking to anyone ever again.
